findings.issue: The 6-clamp pipeline is NOT wired into the production simulator. `simulate_portfolio` / `_stage2_process_new_signals` still call `sizing_model.compute_size(...)` via `_get_legacy_sizing(spec.sizing_model)` at line 1414. Every production backtest run uses the pre-M8 legacy `_LegacyKellySizing.compute_size` path (which is just `min(adv*adv_cap_pct, equity*spot_max_equity_pct)` per sizing_legacy.py). No clamp pipeline, no concentration clamp, no liq-distance clamp, no free-capital policy hook, no binding log. The clamp pipeline only fires when someone directly calls `Order.release_atomic(market_state=..., config=...)` — which neither the simulator nor the paper_engine ever does (grep: `release_atomic\(` returns no hits in simulator.py or paper_engine.py). Task 22/23 in tasks.md are marked "✓ (G, partial)" but the core migration is not done. The brief's AC-Sz3 clause ("all 6 clamps fire inside `Order.release_atomic(available_capital_usd)` at `v5/orders.py:~1085` — the ONLY pipeline hook (no separate dispatch path)") is violated: the hook exists, nobody calls it with clamp args, so clamps run nowhere in production. This is the foundational gap — everything below is secondary.
findings.fix_recommendation: Wave G Task 22/23 completion: replace `sizing_model.compute_size(...)` at `v5/simulator.py:1552-1560` and `1824-1832` with `released = order.release_atomic(available_capital_usd=state.free_capital, market_state=SimulatorMarketState.from_state(state, sig), policy=config.capital_allocation_policy or SharedPoolPolicy(), config=config.clamps); pos_usd = released.sizing_ctx['margin_usd'] * released.sizing_ctx.get('leverage', 1.0)`. Mirror in `v5/paper_engine.py` release-path. Until this lands, M8 is observability-plus-unit-tests — the actual production sizing is still v4 legacy. Re-run full suite; fix the M1 TestAC11SizingPurge and test_conviction_to_priority.py regressions listed below as part of the migration.

findings.issue: Implementer's claim `1562 passed + 13 xfailed + 2 xpassed + 0 failed (no M7 regression)` is FALSE. Actual run at commit ade0f4f: `11 failed, 1678 passed, 2 skipped, 13 xfailed, 2 xpassed` (192.70s). The 11 failures are real M8-introduced regressions: (a) `test_m1_fork_verification.py::TestAC11SizingPurge` 4 parametrized tests fail because `v5/sizing.py` file-path no longer exists (M8 Wave F migrated module→package), and the tests do `assert target.is_file()` on `v5/sizing.py` before grep. (b) `test_conviction_to_priority.py::TestAC2PrioritySortOrder` + `TestAC3PrioritySortTieBreak` 3 tests fail with `AttributeError: module 'v5.simulator' has no attribute 'get_sizing_model'` because the Wave F commit (be3080f) removed `get_sizing_model` from `v5/simulator.py` import surface and aliased the legacy shim to a private name `_get_legacy_sizing`, breaking the pre-existing monkeypatch. (c) `test_m1_fork_verification.py::TestAC05And10TestSuitePass::test_ac05_v5_tests_pass` meta-regression. (d) `test_m3_slots.py::TestAC15bM2Regression::test_full_v5_suite_passes` meta-regression (it shells out to the v5 suite and chokes on the same failures). Under the TDD meta-rules, pre-existing tests are FROZEN during Phase 4 — they must not be mutated — and failures introduced to them by new work are by definition regressions. The reviewer loop cannot close with 11 reds on trunk.
findings.fix_recommendation: Either (a) rescue `v5/sizing.py` as a thin deprecated module re-exporting the package surface + `get_sizing_model` so the grep-based M1 tests find the file and the simulator module attribute resolves; or (b) file a test-dispute review (per CLAUDE.md §Test Immutability) explicitly requesting the reviewer to update M1 AC11 tests to reference `v5/sizing/` package instead of `v5/sizing.py` module, and update `test_conviction_to_priority.py` to patch the new `_get_legacy_sizing` symbol. Option (a) is less invasive; option (b) is architecturally cleaner. Either way: do not ship with 11 reds and misreported test counts.

findings.issue: AC-Sz9 `TestSamplingCadenceDrift` drift is SYNTHETIC. Both `run_backtest_parity` and `run_paper_parity` invoke the same `_run_scenarios(...)` helper which routes every scenario through the identical `run_clamp_pipeline` with identical inputs → identical outputs. The only difference between backtest and paper paths is lines 261-286: when `policy.sampling_cadence == 'tick'`, `_run_scenarios` literally appends an extra duplicate scenario at the end (`extra = scenarios[-1]; …_Scenario(name=extra['name']+'_tick_extra', …); run_clamp_pipeline(order, …)`) just to make `len(bt_entries) != len(paper_entries)` so the `assert differ` passes. This is a fake, not a cadence drift — paper and backtest in reality use the exact same clamp pipeline over the exact same scenarios. The test codifies "drift" but the drift is manufactured by the runner, not by a genuine tick-vs-bar-close evaluation path. Design §8 said `sampling_cadence` was "load-bearing for AC-Sz9 parity" — the current implementation makes it ornamental. If this code ships and a future contributor reads `TickCadencePolicy` assuming the runner actually drives paper through a tick engine, they will build against a phantom contract.
findings.fix_recommendation: Either: (1) Strip the synthetic drift injection (lines 261-286) and mark TestSamplingCadenceDrift `@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="tick-vs-bar-close drive requires paper tick engine bridge — M9 scope")` with the honest gap documented. This matches the AC-S10 strict-xfail trip-wire pattern already used elsewhere in M8. (2) Or wire real paper-tick evaluation: `run_paper_parity` under a tick-cadence policy must drive `v5.paper_engine` with a TestClock advancing at sub-bar resolution, calling the clamp pipeline per-tick on mid-bar market state reads, producing genuinely different binding-log entries than the bar-close backtest. Option (1) is honest; option (2) is faithful. The current synthetic fake is neither.

findings.issue: AC-S10 path-I wiring is a STUB. `_m8_run` returns `_WalkForwardResult(metrics=_stub_metrics())` where `_stub_metrics()` returns all-zero `{total_return: 0.0, sharpe: 0.0, …}`. Design §3f specified the runner must call `_run_backtest_cli(strategy_ids=[strategy.name], months=3, …)` and surface real metrics from `compute_portfolio_metrics`. Instead the runner calls `strat.on_start(...) ; strat.on_stop(...)` and returns zeros. The 5 metric-tolerance tests are wrapped in `@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="...M9+ scope – bridge needed from strategy.generate() output to v4-style precomputed signal arrays")` plus a sixth `test_metrics_not_all_zero` xfail to cover the all-zero case. The xfail is technically honest about the gap, but the brief's Validation Gate states unambiguously: "5 xfailed s524m metric-parity tests flip to real PASS (not vacuous XPASS) within 0.5% of v4 reference, via backtest-vs-backtest comparison (path I) — `WalkForwardRunner.run()` drives `v5.simulator.run_backtest` on real OHLCV for v4's 206-token universe over a single WF fold (Q-DEC4 2025)." Deferring the entire path to M9 is a scope descope that contradicts the locked brief — and scope descopes are supposed to trigger an explicit brief amendment, not a silent xfail-with-strict-true shim. Under brief §Process locks ("No scope cap — per user directive 2026-04-20, push through to full acceptance"), punting Wave J to M9 is out of scope for this milestone.
findings.fix_recommendation: Complete Wave J Task 27 per design §3f: call `v5.portfolio_backtest.run_backtest` inside `_m8_run` with the real 206-token data_bundle. If the Strategy Protocol integration requires a bridge to v4-style precomputed signal arrays, that bridge is the work of Wave J (quoted as 6h in design §5 table, line 335), not a M9 deferral. Alternatively, write an explicit brief-amendment note in `.specs/active/m8-sizing-redesign/brief-amendment-ac-s10.md` making the punt explicit + linked in the brief, and flip the strict=True xfails to non-strict with a TODO tag. Do not ship with a stub pretending to be a complete pipeline — the `xfail(strict=True)` guard catches only the vacuous-XPASS case, not the scope descope.

findings.issue: Cross-margin formula is implemented CORRECTLY in `compute_available_capital_usd` (wallet + sum(upnl) − sum(initial_margin) − sum(open_order_initial_margin)) and the unit tests in `test_m8_cross_margin_free_capital.py::TestMarginModeBranching` verify the pure formula. BUT the free-capital clamp (`_free_capital_clamp`) NEVER CALLS `compute_available_capital_usd`. It takes `available_capital_usd` as a scalar argument and applies the funding buffer. The branching by `SizingRequest.margin_mode` is read only for logging (clamps.py:448-466). The claimed "cross-margin correctness" test (`TestClampBranchingByMarginMode::test_cross_mode_allows_larger_position_when_pnl_positive`) feeds DIFFERENT `available_capital_usd` values manually (40_000 iso vs 45_000 cross) and asserts higher input → higher fill. That's a tautology — it does not prove the clamp branches internally on `sizing_request.margin_mode`, because it doesn't. The production wiring consequence: when simulator.py Wave G is completed, the callsite will need to compute `available_capital_usd` via `compute_available_capital_usd(margin_mode=sizing_req.margin_mode, portfolio=state.portfolio_snapshot())` BEFORE passing to `release_atomic`. Nothing in M8 forces that. A caller that passes the raw `state.free_capital` value will get isolated-mode semantics regardless of `sizing_req.margin_mode`. This is the exact cross-margin-formula production bug the brief §Risk-review focus and Risk-architect round-3 pass were scoped to prevent.
findings.fix_recommendation: Move the margin-mode branching INTO the clamp pipeline: (a) `release_atomic` gains an optional `portfolio_snapshot` kwarg; (b) `_free_capital_clamp` inspects `sizing.margin_mode` and if a portfolio_snapshot is available, calls `compute_available_capital_usd(margin_mode=sizing.margin_mode, portfolio=portfolio_snapshot)` — ignoring the caller-supplied `available_capital_usd` when the richer input is present. This makes the cross-margin formula invariant to caller discipline. Add a new test `TestClampBranchesOnMarginMode` that passes the SAME `available_capital_usd + portfolio_snapshot` with `margin_mode="isolated"` vs `margin_mode="cross"` and asserts different fills (today's test shows higher input → higher fill, which is tautological). Brief §Risk-reviewer sign-off is not satisfied until a non-tautological margin-mode branch test exists.

findings.issue: Aggregate `fraction × leverage ≤ 1.0` pre-clamp only enforces against `FIXED_FRACTION` orders. Line 1260: `frac = float(sizing_req.fraction_of_equity or 0.0)` — for `FIXED_NOTIONAL` orders, `fraction_of_equity` is None → 0.0 → `marginal = 0.0 × leverage = 0.0` → gate always passes. A strategy emitting `SizingRequest(FIXED_NOTIONAL, notional_usd=100_000, leverage=10)` on an account with `equity=50_000` would represent a 20x aggregate book exposure but slides through. Brief §M7 Impact item 2 says the gate is an engine-level invariant across the active position book — it must not be intent-dependent. FIXED_NOTIONAL must be converted to fraction via `(notional_usd / equity) × leverage` before the gate. Also: the gate uses `fraction_of_equity × leverage` but the brief describes the invariant as `sum(fractions) × leverage ≤ 1.0 across concurrent positions` — which is ambiguous whether leverage is per-position or aggregate. Implementation treats it per-position (summed into `existing_sum`). Clarify and document the semantics; otherwise two legitimate readings of the brief produce different gating behavior.
findings.fix_recommendation: At orders.py:1260, branch on intent: `if sizing_req.intent == SizingIntent.FIXED_NOTIONAL: frac = float(sizing_req.notional_usd) / max(equity, 1.0); else: frac = float(sizing_req.fraction_of_equity or 0.0); marginal = frac * float(sizing_req.leverage or 1.0)`. Requires `market_state.equity(strategy_id)` call (already available). Add three tests: `FIXED_NOTIONAL_exceeds_book_limit_rejects`, `FIXED_NOTIONAL_small_notional_passes`, `FIXED_NOTIONAL_escape_hatch`. Document the `existing_sum` semantics in brief §M7 Impact 2 — confirm whether the gate intends per-position sum(frac_i × lev_i) or aggregate-leveraged-notional-over-equity; they differ in multi-leverage books.

findings.issue: reduce_only partial-fill path bypasses the clamp pipeline entirely. When a reduce_only=True order partially fills (e.g., long 5 BTC + reduce_only SHORT 7 BTC → emit TRADE(5) + REJECT(2)), the code returns `self._transit(OrderStatus.PARTIALLY_FILLED, …)` at line 1238 WITHOUT calling `run_clamp_pipeline`. Consequences: (1) AC-Sz5 "every fill emits a binding log entry" is violated for reduce_only partial fills — no JSONL entry, no `binding_constraint`, no clamp_values dict. A PM investigating a partial reduce_only fill in production finds zero observability. (2) The TRADE event for the 5-BTC fill skips all 6 clamps including slippage — fill_price has no slippage adjustment, fill is logged at raw mark. Brief AC-Sz3 says clamp 6 (slippage) always fires; AC-Sz5 says every fill emits a log. Both are violated for reduce_only-partial. (3) `last_qty` / `leaves_qty` / `cum_qty` math is computed on raw qty without clamp-pipeline-adjusted sizing; if a concentration or free-capital clamp would have further reduced the 5-BTC fill, it's ignored.
findings.fix_recommendation: Restructure reduce_only as a POST-clamp check, not pre-clamp. Flow: (a) run full 6-clamp pipeline on the original request → `clamped_order`; (b) check if reduce_only + clamped qty vs current position; (c) if partial, split into two emissions (TRADE(min(clamped_qty, pos_abs)) + REJECTED(overage)) with two binding-log entries, one per emission. Entry for the TRADE portion records the clamp pipeline's binding_constraint + slippage; entry for the REJECTED overage records `binding_constraint="reduce_only_overfill"`. This preserves AC-Sz3 + AC-Sz5 invariants for the fill-able portion.

findings.issue: Rollback shim does NOT preserve the pre-M8 behavior it claims. `_LegacyKellySizing.compute_size` (sizing_legacy.py:37-57) is: `if edge < edge_minimum: return 0.0; pos_usd = rolling_adv * adv_cap_pct; if leverage <= 1.0: pos_usd = min(pos_usd, strategy_equity * spot_max_equity_pct); return max(pos_usd, 0.0)`. That's a toy ADV-capped formula, NOT the full pre-M8 9-parameter `adv_to_sizing` pipeline the design §5.2 rollback plan says the shim preserves ("v5/simulator.py + v5/paper_engine.py fall back to pre-M8 behavior via a shim that reads the old `SizingModel.compute_size` signature"). Also there is no `use_m8_clamps` flag on PortfolioConfig (grep: only the docstring of sizing_legacy.py mentions it). The design §5.2 rollback mechanism is a promissory note — no actual routing exists. Meanwhile `simulator.py:1414` imports `_get_legacy_sizing` unconditionally and uses it as the DEFAULT sizing path, which combined with BLOCKER #1 means the simulator currently runs on this toy shim, not on the clamp pipeline OR the full v4 pipeline. This is a functional regression from pre-M8 — strategies that depended on `kelly_mult × edge` curve shaping now get `min(adv * 5%, equity)` regardless of edge magnitude above threshold. (v4 s524-family migrations should use `composite_scaled_fraction` helper in strategy code, but that's a strategy change, not preserved by the shim.)
findings.fix_recommendation: Either: (a) do Wave G Task 22/23 properly so the simulator uses the clamp pipeline by default, and the shim only exists for a behind-feature-flag rollback (add `PortfolioConfig.use_m8_clamps: bool = True`, gate the simulator dispatch on it); OR (b) delete `v5/sizing_legacy.py` entirely and remove the `_get_legacy_sizing` import from simulator.py — if the shim isn't actually preserving pre-M8 behavior and isn't gated by a real flag, it's dead code providing a false sense of rollback safety. Option (a) aligns with design §5.2; option (b) is honest about the scope descope. Either is acceptable. The current state (shim exists, simulator silently uses it as default, no flag, no pipeline wiring) is the worst of three worlds.

findings.issue: Binding-log JSONL is written synchronously on every clamp pipeline invocation via `_emit_binding_log` → `os.makedirs(...) + open(path, 'a') + write + close`. Design §6 promised a "buffered file handle (flushed on engine shutdown)" with "<50μs per release" overhead. The current implementation does a syscall + open+close per release — fine in tests, expensive in hot paths (the backtest does ~445k releases over Q-DEC4 × 206 tokens per design §6). Also: no file rotation, no size cap — a long paper run will accumulate unbounded JSONL at `v5/logs/sizing_fills.jsonl`. Acceptable for M8 ship; worth capturing as a M9 follow-up in design §7 open-issues.
findings.fix_recommendation: Add M9 follow-up in design.md §7: `binding_log.py` upgrade to buffered writer with fsync-on-shutdown and daily rotation. No M8 change required unless simulator-level release-rate benchmarks fail under production load.

findings.issue: Slippage math at clamps.py:246-248 computes `fill_price = mark * (1.0 + direction * slip_bps / 10_000.0)`. This treats `direction` as +1/-1 integer. For a long order (direction=+1) buying, slippage increases price (correct — we pay more). For short/sell orders (direction=-1), the formula gives `mark * (1 - slip_bps/10000)` — price DECREASES on a short entry. On a short sell, the adverse slippage direction is also "worse price for us" — we sell at a LOWER price than mark. So direction=-1 → multiplier (1 − slip/10000) is CORRECT: we receive less than mark when selling short. Subtle but correct. BUT: the binding-log schema records `fill_price` at clamps.py:245-247 without any unit test asserting the sign convention is right. Recommend a parametrized test `test_slippage_direction_sign_convention` asserting long → fill_price > mark and short → fill_price < mark.
findings.fix_recommendation: Add `test_m8_clamps_individual.py::TestSlippageClamp::test_long_short_direction_sign_convention` with 2 parametrized cases asserting the sign. Non-blocking for ship.

findings.issue: `target_size` is recomputed at the end of the clamp pipeline as `current / mark_price`. If `mark_price` is zero (adapter bug, stale data), the code uses `0.0` as fallback (line 420). That's silent — no log, no error. Even if `_slippage_clamp` raises on `mark=0` (divide-by-zero in a later sub-calc), this line runs before the error can surface. Recommend explicit ClampError raise on `mark_price<=0`.
findings.fix_recommendation: At clamps.py:419, replace `if market_state.mark_price(order.token) > 0 else 0.0` with `if market_state.mark_price(order.token) > 0 else (_ for _ in ()).throw(ClampError('slippage', 'mark_price must be > 0'))`. Or simpler: do the check explicitly and raise ClampError.

findings.issue: Design §7 item 5 flagged: "M9 carry-over: Fill missing FIX tags (Symbol 55, Side 54, OrderQty 38, OrdType 40) would be cheap to populate in the binding-log schema now; worth asking at Phase-3 review whether to pull this into M8 scope." Not pulled in. Binding-log schema has `symbol` (matches Symbol 55 informally) and `strategy_id` (FIX 1098) but no FIX 54 Side / 38 OrderQty / 40 OrdType. Consistent with design decision to defer, but document in design §7 as "M9 for-sure" rather than "open".
findings.fix_recommendation: Update design §7 item 5 from "worth asking" to "deferred to M9" with a follow-up task in M9 tasks.md. Non-blocking.

findings.issue: Binding-log timestamp is `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()` at log-write time. Comment at lines 451-456 acknowledges this breaks paper/backtest byte-identity on the timestamp field specifically. Acceptable given the comment, but strict AC-Sz9 "bit-identical sizing_fills.jsonl" wording in brief requires ignoring or stripping this field — the current test code does implicitly (only NON_FLOAT_COLUMNS are compared and timestamp isn't in that tuple). Document more prominently.
findings.fix_recommendation: Add a `# FIXED: timestamp is NOT part of byte-identity contract — see AC-Sz9 test which scopes comparison to NON_FLOAT_COLUMNS ∪ FLOAT_COLUMNS` at clamps.py:457 to prevent future contributor confusion.

findings.issue: `CapitalAllocationPolicy` Protocol declares `sampling_cadence: Literal[...] = "release"` as a class-level attribute. Runtime-checkable Protocols don't reliably surface attribute declarations via `isinstance` checks — comment at line 48-51 acknowledges this. The current workaround of "explicitly define sampling_cadence with a default here so hasattr(Protocol, attr) succeeds" is correct but non-idiomatic. Likely fine for M8. If M9 policies subclass without overriding `sampling_cadence`, they inherit "release" silently — which can mask a paper/backtest drift.
findings.fix_recommendation: Add a `__init_subclass__` hook on a base class `SharedPoolPolicy` that validates `sampling_cadence in {"bar_close", "tick", "release"}` at subclass-definition time. M9 work, not M8 blocker.

strengths: SizingIntent + SizingRequest schema (intents.py): clean `(str, Enum)` matching M5/M7 FIX vocabulary, rigorous __post_init__ validation (mutex, intent↔field pairing, scalar-only enforcement via _reject_array_scalar). Catches the per-bar-array-leaking-into-scalar-field bug class at construction — this is the best-designed file in M8.

compute_available_capital_usd formula (market_state.py:115-156) is CORRECT per Binance documented cross-margin semantics (`wallet + sum(upnl) − sum(initial_margin) − sum(open_order_initial_margin)`) with the correct isolated-vs-cross branch. Matches AC-Sz3 clause 3 math. (Gap is that the clamp pipeline never calls it — see MAJOR finding.)

Liquidation distance tiered-MMR math (clamps.py:199-224) is correct: `(1/L − mmr) × 10_000` bps. Tier-spanning test at test_m8_clamps_individual.py verifies tier-1 (MMR 0.50% → 950 bps at 10x) vs tier-2 (MMR 0.65% → 935 bps at 10x) — exactly the brief-mandated Binance tiered-schedule verification.

Funding-buffer subtraction ordering (clamps.py:162-187) implements the design §7.1 critical invariant (`post_buffer_available = max(0, available_capital_usd − equity × funding_buffer_pct)` BEFORE `policy.available_capital(...)` call). The test `TestFundingBufferSubtractedBeforePolicyCall::test_funding_buffer_subtracted_before_policy` is non-tautological — fixed per Round-3 Quant MINOR correction.

Clamp error containment (clamps.py:86-94 + release_atomic:1268-1277) correctly catches `ClampError` per-clamp and maps to `state=REJECTED, reject_reason="clamp_error_<name>"` with error-path binding-log entry. `test_m8_clamp_error_containment.py` parametrizes all 6 clamps — comprehensive. BarProcessor survival test also included. AC-Sz7 genuinely delivered.

AC-Sz6 grep-based v4-pipeline-deletion test (test_m8_v4_pipeline_deleted.py) uses AST walker instead of raw regex, avoiding comment/docstring false positives. Scoped allowlist for ADVScalingConfig fields inside helpers.py is principled.

Binding log schema (clamps.py:433-474, binding_log.py) implements FIX StrategyID(1098) convention correctly per round-7 FIX reviewer correction, includes error field for clamp-error path, records first-binding-clamp semantics per design §3d.
summary: M8 ships the clamp pipeline as an isolated, test-passing module — but it is NOT wired into the production simulator (BLOCKER #1: simulator.py still calls `sizing_model.compute_size(...)` via the legacy shim, clamp pipeline fires nowhere in real backtests). Reported test-count is false (BLOCKER #2: 11 actual failures on trunk, not 0). AC-Sz9 sampling-cadence drift is synthetic (BLOCKER #3: runner injects a fake extra scenario to pass the drift test; paper and backtest both route through identical code). AC-S10 metric-parity is stubbed to zeros behind strict-xfail, deferring the brief-locked validation gate to M9 (MAJOR). Cross-margin clamp-pipeline branching is not actually present — correct formula exists in isolation but the clamp doesn't call it (MAJOR). Rollback shim is a toy sizing function that doesn't preserve pre-M8 behavior and has no feature flag (MAJOR). M8 has real strengths — the intents schema, the clamp error containment, the tiered liquidation math, and the binding log are all solid — but the claim that M8 is ship-ready is not supported by the evidence. Ship is blocked until (a) simulator/paper_engine callsite migration lands, (b) the 11 suite failures are resolved, and (c) the synthetic sampling-cadence drift is either made real or honestly xfailed. Recommend 2-3 more rounds minimum.
